PREFIX brick: <https://brickschema.org/schema/1.2/brick#>
PREFIX ref: <https://brickschema.org/schema/1.2/ref#>
SELECT ?zone ?label ?point ?pclass ?tsid WHERE {
  ?zone brick:hasPoint ?point .
  ?zone rdfs:label ?label .
  FILTER (regex(?label, "Core_z|Core_bottom|Core_mid|Core_top Zone", "i") || contains(str(?zone),"Zone_F2_Z01") || contains(str(?zone),"Zone_F3") || contains(str(?zone),"Zone_F4"))
  ?point brick:a ?pclass .
  ?point ref:hasTimeseriesId ?tsid .
} LIMIT 200

PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
SELECT ?point ?pclass ?tsid ?slabel WHERE {
  ?zone rdfs:label ?slabel .
  FILTER(CONTAINS(str(?zone),"Zone_F2_Z01"))
  ?zone ?has ?point .
  ?point rdf:type ?pclass .
  ?point ref:hasTimeseriesId ?tsid
} LIMIT 200

content.text: The data distinguishes clearly: the occupied-hours **scheduled** setpoint stream (Occupied_Air_Temperature_Cooling_Setpoint) remained essentially unchanged (~24.46 °C both before and after mid-June), yet during occupied hours the **actual applied** zone cooling setpoint (Zone_Air_Cooling_Temperature_Setpoint) dropped ~1 °C (24.46 → 23.49) and the sensor temperature fell ~1 °C too. Since the schedule was unchanged but the applied setpoint deviated from it, this is consistent with a local override / controller offset, not a schedule change.
